restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..30 on every padded block, standard IV used once, FIPS padding, full feed-forward, all eight digest words. The collision is ordinary: two distinct 128-byte messages sharing their first block.
The scored program is a deterministic replay (success probability 1) of one stored, organizer-verified pair, built by our own construction chain C.

C uses no published colliding pair, starting solution or first block. Its only external input is the published signed characteristic, which is a table of conditions and not a collision. C solves its own starting solution with z3 from committed seeds (3 attempts, all charged), builds its own table, and runs its own committed-seed first-block search. Runs that read the published pair or the starting solution derived from it (the relaxed-search, synthetic and K' runs, and the analysis runs analyze.py and table, which filings up to v9 charged) are excluded from C and fixed no constant of C (proof.md Sections 15.1 and 15.4).

Total time is the executed work of C. The z3 attempts are charged at 7 primitive word operations per retired instruction, priced from profiles of every executed instruction of the same solver on the same models, with every multiply, divide and floating-point form at the tariff of a checked emulation (proof.md Section 14). Search K and the three synthetic checks are charged by exact operation counts of explicit word-RAM programs that reproduce their executables' decisions, the stored pair and the runs' logged counters (Section 16). The analysis programs that formulated R20 are charged by exact counts of counted versions with identical outputs (Section 15.2). With the other own code and the 6.36-unit replay, that is 42,877,883,846 = 2^35.3195 units. Every premise is a declared heuristic (H1-H8). The full source, the emulation checks and the commitments are in the proof appendices.
Memory is a reported metric only. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: The published 31-step signed characteristic (the condition table of proof.md Section 5 and the differences d5..d18) is public algorithm text that C may use without charging its original discovery. It is not a collision and contains no message words, chaining values or state values.
heuristics.scope: The characteristic only. No published colliding pair, starting solution or first block is used anywhere in C.
heuristics.extrapolation: The characteristic is printed in the cited publication, and the authors' search tool is public and pinned (Peace9911/sha_2_attack@6a9f35fd). Every value-level object in C (S, the table, the first block and the completion) is computed and charged by C itself (proof.md Sections 7-9).
heuristics.limitations: The trail search is not executed or bounded by our own evidence in this filing. A charge of T units adds T to the 42,877,883,846-unit total; the total stays below 2^39.15 for T up to 2^39.04 and below 2^40.4 for T up to 2^40.35.

heuristics.statement: The work of search K, of the three synthetic completion checks and of the pre-construction analysis programs is the operation count of explicit programs that compute the same results with collision-frontier-v5 primitives (proof.md Sections 15.2 and 16), not the retired instructions of their executables. K: 582 primitives per trial, 4,677 per pass of 8 trials, worst-path counts per event times the run's counters. Synthetic checks: exact counted replays. Analysis: exact counts of counted versions.
heuristics.scope: kprog.py, kcount.c, scount.c and pcount.c (proof Appendix C.6-C.9, C.13) and the runs they charge.
heuristics.extrapolation: The counted programs use only v5 primitives on values in their own 256-bit words, count every load and store, use no native 32-bit rotation and write Sigma, sigma, Ch and Maj as exact identities; their 64-bit products are explicit 385-primitive emulations. K's program agrees with r31det3 on every key, bitmap decision and hit counter of 71,670,492 trials and reproduces the stored pair; the synthetic replays agree trial by trial with r31sim3's process_sim and reproduce the logged FINAL counters; the counted analysis programs print the originals' outputs.
heuristics.limitations: With the forms of our previous filing (775 per trial) the total would be 2^35.594; with the reference core's forms (1035), 2^35.896; with twice every K line, 2^36.032; with twice the synthetic checks, 2^35.383; with the analysis at our earlier hand bounds (which covered the excluded table runs), 2^35.634; with K charged by its executable's instructions, 2^36.115 or 2^36.860.

heuristics.statement: Every multiply, divide and floating-point instruction is priced by an explicit emulation in v5 primitives: 32-bit-operand multiplies 210, 64-bit multiplies 392 (umulh 392, smulh 408), udiv/sdiv 360/384 (w) and 712/736 (x), binary64 add 240, multiply 520, fused multiply-add 600, divide 824, square root 1008, compare 48, int-to-double 152, double-to-int 24. Ordinary forms follow the per-form rules of a64ops.py (proof.md Section 14.2).
heuristics.scope: The pricing of z3's executed instructions and the floating-point operations of the counted analysis programs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Each tariff is the largest primitive count of its emulation (mul32.py, heavy.py, proof Appendix C.11) on the checked inputs, rounded up to a multiple of 8. The checks compare every emulation with the instruction's definition (integers; the host's IEEE binary64 arithmetic; exact fractions for fused multiply-add) on 20,000 integer and 100,000 floating-point cases per form, including zeros, subnormals, infinities and NaNs. The emulations have fixed-count loops and a few data-dependent paths, which the checked inputs exercise.
heuristics.limitations: With every heavy tariff doubled the total would be 2^35.524; with the v5 table's uniform 400 and 1024, 2^35.442.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory over C and the pre-construction analysis is at most 2^29.5 bytes.
heuristics.scope: Every charged run (proof.md Section 15.1): z3 attempts, search K, synthetic checks, yield checks, V8 dump, c8 scan, the analysis programs (sets, joint, pany, pany2), the Python runs, and the excluded table runs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Maximum resident set sizes from /usr/bin/time -l (proof.md Section 10): recorded during the charged runs for z3 and K, from re-runs of the same binaries on the same inputs for the rest. The largest is joint, 538,050,560 bytes = 2^29.003, explained by its source: two calloc'd hash tables of 2^25 entries of 8 bytes (2^29 bytes). 2^29.5 bytes is 1.41 times that peak.
heuristics.limitations: Resident set size counts touched pages; the claim leaves 1.41x headroom over the measured peak and covers every source's allocations. Memory does not enter the score.

heuristics.statement: Every constant of C comes from the public characteristic, from analysis, from the charged pre-construction analysis programs, or from the charged v3 runs before K (proof.md Section 15.3). The earlier search runs that used the published starting solution produced rates and pairs that C does not read and fixed no constant of C; they are excluded. The three analyze.py runs and the two table runs of the pre-construction analysis read the published pair or the starting solution derived from it; they are excluded as well, and their outputs are either functions of the characteristic itself or unused (proof.md Section 15.4).
heuristics.scope: All computation on this target in our working directories and session records on 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07, listed in proof.md Section 15.1.
heuristics.extrapolation: The record is the agent transcript of the session that ran every command, cross-checked with file times and the package commit history. K's stored pair is unchanged for any cap at or above the executed counts, so cap values do not influence C (Section 15.4). The commitments are local, not notarised.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer charged the excluded 2^40.625-trial search run anyway, the total would be 2^40.682.

heuristics.statement: The per-form mix measured on the Linux build of z3 4.15.4 (PyPI z3-solver 4.15.4.0) bounds the per-form mean of the macOS binary that ran; the z3 price 7 is charged on the macOS instruction counts.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every profiled run repeats the charged search (same model, rlimit-count, conflicts and decisions). The two builds have the same static profile, and both compile about 90% of their multiply sites to 32-bit-operand forms. The macOS build retires more instructions for the same searches (attempt 1: 261,276,415,067 against 245,527,956,010; attempt 2: 1,572,256,055,396 against 1,475,640,959,576; attempt 3: 888,282,131,643 against 834,226,129,830) with the same multiplies and divides.
heuristics.limitations: Not an identical instruction mix. With the z3 price doubled the total would be 2^35.592; at 19, 2^35.758; at 256, 2^38.386.

heuristics.statement: The instruction profiles of z3 attempts 2 and 3 are reconstructed from exp-bbv superblock counts, because callgrind's memory grows without bound on these runs. Each superblock is disassembled from the executable that ran (to the first control transfer or 100 instructions).
heuristics.scope: z3 attempts 2 and 3 (proof.md Section 14.4); attempt 1 is priced from its complete callgrind profile.
heuristics.extrapolation: On attempt 1 the reconstruction gives a whole-run mean of 5.0436 against callgrind's 5.0356 and a largest interval of 5.3589 against 5.3503. Superblocks whose count is not a multiple of their length (5.01% of the instructions) are charged at the largest prefix mean ending at one of their branches, an upper bound for any mix of exits; the final partial intervals (1,867,089,404 instructions) are charged at 1024.
heuristics.limitations: With the bounded superblocks at twice their bound and the final intervals at 4096 per instruction, the total would be 2^35.412.

heuristics.statement: Library calls of the counted programs' runs are bounded by 10^5 instructions per call at 1024 each; the Python runs by a lump allowance of 1e9 units; the yield checks, the V8 dump and the c8 residue scan by hand bounds from source (24 per scanned word, 64 per table candidate, 8 per residue candidate).
heuristics.scope: The corresponding lines of proof.md Sections 9, 15.2, 16.3 and 16.6 (3.5% of the total).
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured re-runs of comparable runs (gen_s.py and check_s.py retire 2.2e8 instructions each) and the source of the programs; library-call instruction counts are not measured individually.
heuristics.limitations: With ten times every library-call bound and twice the Python lump and the hand bounds, the total would be 2^35.500.
